name: Diaminopyrimidine oxide

lead: Diaminopyrimidine oxide is an ingredient in some hair-growth lotions, described as minoxidil-like.
Sources reviewed are mainly cosmetic patents; no trials testing it were found.

paras: Patents say such compositions enhance hair root activity; no mechanism data were found.
No safety data were found in the reviewed sources.

trials.title: A Scalp Lotion Toimprove Sensitive Scalp Syndrome

lead: Diaminopyrimidine oxide is a minoxidil-related ingredient that appears in some hair-growth and anti-hair-loss lotions and shampoos. In the sources reviewed, it appears mainly in cosmetic patents, including Korean patent filings from 2007 and 2008 describing compositions of pyrrolidinyl diaminopyrimidine oxide for hair growth and for preventing hair loss.[1][2]

A 2026 systematic review and network meta-analysis compared off-label and unregulated therapies for male androgenetic alopecia beyond minoxidil.[3] No randomized clinical trial of diaminopyrimidine oxide was found in the reviewed sources.

paras: A 2008 Korean patent describes a hair-loss prevention composition containing henna extract, copper peptide and pyrrolidinyl diaminopyrimidine oxide, stating that it is intended to promote growth by enhancing hair root activity and thickening hair.[2] These are patent claims, not trial results.

No studies found. A registered trial of a scalp lotion for sensitive scalp syndrome (NCT05630027, 100 participants) is listed, but the sources reviewed do not state that it tested this compound.[4] A 2026 network meta-analysis of therapies beyond minoxidil in male androgenetic alopecia is the closest published review.[3]
